policy: Read security-guidance.md and supplied immutable threat model. SECURITY.md resolver returned no inherited policy for assigned runtime, test, hosted-script, or supporting runner directories.

candidates.title: Repeated asset URL literals cause quadratic synchronous work in the shared editor
candidates.attacker_controlled_source: An authenticated project author controls admitted JavaScript modules. A retained array or other used expression can contain many copies of one HTTPS .png URL; multiple allowed modules contribute to the compiled JavaScript artifact.
candidates.broken_control: The AST walk adds an edit per literal without an edit-count budget. The Set on line 136 deduplicates only outbound fetches; repeated literals therefore consume one request/cache entry rather than the 48-resource budget. Line 138 rebuilds the growing full artifact for every edit using slices and concatenation. There is no yield, work budget, or killable worker around this loop.
candidates.sink_and_impact: compileWithRuntime invokes materialize in the shared hosted editor process. O(edit count * artifact size) synchronous string rewriting can monopolize its event loop and cause large transient allocation pressure, delaying authorization, session handling and preview work for other tenants. The 10-second setTimeout abort cannot interrupt synchronous rewriting.
candidates.plausibility: The compiler admits up to 2 MiB per source file and 40 MiB aggregate and returns in-memory browser bundles. Tens of thousands of duplicate string literals fit inside one accepted file. The attacker needs only one public server serving a small valid image; no SSRF bypass or runner execution is needed for this host-side computation.
closest_controls_and_counterevidence: Static resources have a 48-fetch limit, 2 MiB response limit, 8 MiB aggregate transfer limit, 4 materializations/connections and a 10-second asynchronous deadline; these bound network work but not the number of edits for a cached URL.
Source/compiler and final snapshot byte limits exist. These provide finite input sizes but still allow many repeated literals; the final snapshot limit is checked after rewriting.
The entry is retired on error and runner egress remains denied. These controls do not isolate synchronous editor CPU work.

No runtime reproduction was performed. Validation should confirm that an ordinarily compiled, live array preserves enough duplicate literals after minification and quantify shared-event-loop delay at admitted sizes. Avoid claiming process termination without measurement.

negativeReasoning.family: SSRF, reserved IPs, DNS rebinding, redirects
negativeReasoning.evidence: staticAssets.ts:15-21 normalizes HTTPS URLs and rejects credentials, nonstandard ports, IPv6/literal private IPs and sensitive query names. Lines 80-90 resolve and validate every redirect hop, and line 28 pins the validated IPv4 answers in the TLS request lookup without replacing the hostname. externalSource.ts:18-21 denies loopback/private/link-local/CGNAT/documentation/benchmark/multicast/reserved IPv4 ranges. No reachable private-address bypass identified.

staticAssets.ts:28 uses fixed GET/header values, agent:false, no cookie/auth/proxy forwarding, and identity encoding. Lines 30-37 bound headers, response bytes and request time; lines 76-89 bound request count, recursion, redirects and aggregate bytes. Lines 80/84 use abort races and recheck before later requests. Slow/unsettled DNS underlying OS work is not cancelled, but no distinct reportable exhaustion tuple was established beyond the concrete synchronous-rewrite candidate.

staticAssets.ts:40-55 permits only UTF-8 CSS or finite image/font MIME/signature pairs; remote HTML, script and SVG MIME are refused. Remote CSS resources re-enter the URL/DNS checks and recursive fetch limits (103-128), including rejection of remote SVG data images. Finite CSS matching may miss escaped/protocol-relative or other browser resource syntax, but those remaining URLs do not reach the trusted fetcher and the runner's OS no-egress boundary remains intact.

staticAssets.ts:69-70 makes each cache snapshot-local; keys include expected kind and URL, resource filenames hash transformed bytes, and audit includes project/revision (95-100,153). snapshotPreview at controlledPreview.ts:28-38 checks filenames/size and hashes the complete artifact. PostgresArtifactStore at postgresStores.ts:199-231 binds workspace/project/revision/generation/digest, checks preview authority around retrieval and verifies immutable content. No cross-tenant URL cache or mutable shared artifact entry was introduced.

controlledPreview.ts:158-167 checks live project/capability/revision around runtime-value acquisition and compilation; staticAssets.ts:63,68,74,80,85,151 checks before cache/fetch and after async work. Entry retirement aborts the signal (:123-124). hostedProjectRegistry.ts:119-125 and postgresSourceCheckout.ts:39-41 verify fresh capability and exact durable epoch/revision after the callback. Start/update also recheck before returning and after runner work. No distinct reachable stale-grant or stale-source fetch bypass was identified.

publicRuntimeValues.ts:5-18 accepts finite secret-screened plain values with bounded VITE names/count/length; :20-29 checks authority and signal before/after a timed provider call. ConfiguredPublicRuntimeValues at :33-42 is operator-installed and keyed by exact workspace/project; editor-main.ts:14-17 obtains it only from operator config. Hosted session inspection uses grant-derived scope at hostedEditor.ts:125-133 and runtime compilation uses PG-derived sessionOwner at controlledPreview.ts:163. No client/example/host-env fallback or cross-project lookup was found.

The static pass parses JavaScript with the TypeScript AST and CSS with PostCSS; it does not evaluate uploaded modules. Malicious browser source remains inside the existing raster runner. controlledPreview.ts:201 retains external:'deny'; worker.cjs:36-38 verifies the flag and artifact digest and :63-73 serves only job-local artifacts. launch.sh:16 uses bwrap --unshare-all with no network-sharing override. Native browser sandbox checks remain at worker.cjs:51-56.

phase2-breadth-assets.test.ts covers unsafe URLs/DNS, pins, redirects, MIME/signature/compression/size, DNS deadline, revocation, cycles, concurrency and remote SVG. phase2-breadth-values.test.ts covers finite values, secret rejection, post-provider reauthorization, exact tenant pair and canonical/example-source preservation. No test bounds repeated compiled URL edit count or synchronous rewrite time.

execution: Read-only frozen git-object inspection; no source application, uploaded code, runner, VM, tests, network or scan tools executed. Only this discovery JSON was written.
